annotations.title: Is this ſuch a faſt, as I haue choſen.
annotations.text: Faſting is ſo often & clerly commended in holie Scriptures, that Proteſtantes (though not greatly affected therto) confeſſe it to be a good thing of it ſelf, [1] but in diuers reſpectes detract much from it: [2] denying it to be an act of religion, but only of bodily mortification: neither do al generally allow of preſcript times, nor of abſtinence from flesh thoſe dayes, vvhich they thinke good to faſt: and thoſe vvhich do abſtaine from flesh, ſay they do it not for religion, but for the ordinance of ciuil policie. For which opinion they allege out of this, and other places (Iere. 14. v. 12. Zacha. 7. v. 5.) that ſuch affliction is not the faſt, which God hath choſen. But if they vvould conſider the coherence of the text, they ſhould finde the contrarie. For albeit faſting alone vvithout amendment of euil maners, and vvithout other good vvorkes, doth not appeaze Gods vvrath, nor is agreable to Gods vvil, yet being ioyned with contrition of hart, and ſincere pietie, doth then greatly pleaſe him. And therfore our Lord God here (ſayth S. Ierom) leſt he might ſeme to reproue faſting, [3] vvhich himſelf had commanded, teacheth how it behoueth to faſt: [4] Non enim quærit Deus afflictionem ſolam, & humiliationem animæ per iniuriam corporis, vt inſtar circuli torqueat corpus, & colla ſubmittat, ac triſtis incedat: &c. Sed vt cum iſtis hæc faciat quæ ſequuntur. For God ſeeketh not onlie affliction, and humiliation of the ſoule by iniurie of the bodie; that one ſhould vvrith his bodie about like a circle, hold dovvne his neck, and goe penſiue, &c. But that vvith theſe thinges, he do thoſe which [5] folovv: towitte, Diſſolue the bandes of impietie, and the reſt, as in the text. VVherupon this Doctor diſcourſeth at large, shewing that it profiteth not to carie an emptie bellie, and do thoſe thinges that diſpleaſe God. But faſting from meate, ſo that faſting from ſinne (by declining from euil, and doing good deedes) be ioyned withal: then (ſaith he) thy faſting vvil be acceptable: For then shal thy light breake forth as the morning, and thy health shal ſooner ariſe, and thy iuſtice shal goe before thy face, and the glorie of our Lord shal embrace thee. Further declaring the great profite therof by examples: [6] that by faſting Daniel, the man of deſires knew thinges to come: the Niniuites pacified the vvrath of God. Elias and Moyſes by fourtie dayes hunger were filled with the familiaritie of God: [7] And our Lord him ſelf faſted ſo manie dayes in the vvildernes, vt nobis ſolennes ieiuniorum dies relinqueret, to leaue vnto vs the ſolemne dayes of faſtes.

notes.text: Protestants detract from the praise & profite of fasting.
This scripture reproueth not fasting, but admonisheth to fast especially from sinne.
Christs fast an example of the 40. dayes fast in Lent.
